page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-1xL40S is a KVM-hypervised virtual server configured with an AMD EPYC 9575F processor on the x86_64 architecture. The system features 16 vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with a single thread per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding 12.0 GB per core. Acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA L40S GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, which includes 48 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is not bundled with this server configuration, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, placing in the top 10% for stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and bzip3 single-threaded decompression. Multi-core performance is strong, ranking in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU tests. Memory performance is robust, with large-block read and write bandwidths scoring in the top 25%. For specialized workloads, the NVIDIA L40S GPU delivers top-tier prompt processing and text generation speeds on small LLM models, while maintaining strong text generation performance on medium models and average performance on large models.

From a resource density perspective, the server offers high memory-to-vCPU allocation alongside a high-end workstation-class GPU, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring substantial GPU memory without the overhead of multi-GPU clusters. However, the shared CPU allocation and lack of local storage represent key architectural tradeoffs to consider. This configuration is highly suited for machine learning inference, small-to-medium LLM deployment, image processing, data science pipelines, and GPU-accelerated rendering tasks.
description: The UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-1xL40S is a KVM-based virtual server designed for GPU-accelerated workloads. It features an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with 16 vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 192.0 GB of system memory. Graphics and compute acceleration are handled by a single NVIDIA L40S GPU with 48 GB of VRAM on the Ada Lovelace architecture. While local storage is absent, the server delivers top-tier single-core CPU performance and strong multi-core capabilities, alongside high large-block memory bandwidth. In LLM inference benchmarks, it achieves top-tier speeds for small models and strong text generation for medium models. This hardware profile makes the server highly suitable for machine learning inference, image processing, and data science workloads that require significant VRAM and memory capacity without the need for local storage.
